rounds.text: DMR Engineering Ltd is materially mispriced by the market, trading at a modest share price of ₹ 32.0 [E2] while offering a robust discounted cash flow intrinsic value of ₹ 72 per share, which leaves a massive margin of safety of 55.7% [E36]. The market's pessimism is entirely disconnected from underlying fundamentals, as demonstrated by a reverse DCF showing that the current price prices in a paltry 6.9% earnings growth against a base-case assumption of 18.0% [E37]. Operational profitability and capital efficiency are exceptionally strong, highlighted by a stellar ROCE of 19.92% compared to a sector benchmark of just 6.61% [E10], alongside a comfortable short-term liquidity profile with a current ratio of 4.72x [E30]. Furthermore, the company is practically debt-free with borrowings having been reduced to ₹ 0.29 Cr in September 2026 from ₹ 0.67 Cr a year earlier [E31], [E42], and recent quarterly results display a dramatic acceleration featuring a 34% operating margin in September 2026 compared to 22% in the year-ago quarter [E23]. Conceded: trailing twelve months compounded profit growth stands at -36% and the yearly operating-margin trend has been decreasing over the last four years [E17], [E24].

The business faces severe fundamental deterioration in its core growth and cash generation, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of -36% [E17] and a sharp slowdown in annual sales growth to just 1% [E15]. This top and bottom-line strain coincides with a structural contraction in operating margins, which have steadily decreased over the last four years [E24] and dropped by 8 percentage points from three years earlier [E22]. Furthermore, reported profits completely disconnect from actual liquidity, evidenced by a dismal cash conversion ratio of 0.27x and negative free cash flow of Rs -0.30 Cr for March 2026 [E26, E28]. Operational efficiency is further compromised by alarmingly high debtor days of 171 days [E43], signaling acute working capital risks that make earnings quality highly suspect. Compounded share price growth has cratered by -41% over the past year [E19], and promoter holdings have steadily dwindled by 2.56 percentage points since December 2021 [E33]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.02x along with strong historical three-year sales and profit growth [E14, E16, E29].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth sits at -36% [E17], annual sales growth slowed to 1% [E15], and debtor days are high at 171 [E43]. However, focusing solely on trailing metrics ignores a powerful cyclical turnaround and accelerating current performance, evidenced by quarterly operating margins surging by +12 percentage points to 34% in September 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E23]. The bear's alarm over margin erosion [E22, E24] is outdated when results score a perfect 100/100 with net profit soaring +183% year-over-year, proving that recent sentiment and share price drops of -41% are anchored to stale data rather than current realities [E39, E49]. Furthermore, cash generation concerns [E26, E28] are mitigated by positive operating cash flow of Rs 0.46 Cr [E27], an exceptionally comfortable current ratio of 4.72x [E30], and a pristine balance sheet featuring near-zero debt of Rs 0.29 Cr down from a year earlier [E29, E31, E42]. Finally, the minor promoter stake reduction [E33] does not undermine a robust multi-year foundation that includes a 42% three-year sales growth rate [E14] and a superior ROCE of 19.92% crushing the sector benchmark of 6.61% [E10].

Conceded: quarterly operating margins surged to 34% in September 2026 [E23]. However, the bull's dismissal of margin concerns is countered by a yearly operating-margin trend that reads decreasing over the last four years and a TTM margin drop of eight percentage points [E22, E24]. Conceded: operating cash flow was positive at Rs 0.46 Cr [E27]. Yet the bull ignores that free cash flow was negative at Rs -0.30 Cr [E28], cash conversion sits at a concerning 0.27x where profits far outpace cash [E26], and the company is saddled with high debtors of 171 days [E43]. Conceded: debt has been reduced [E41, E42], but the bull glosses over the multi-year deceleration where trailing twelve-month sales growth slowed to 1% [E15] and compounded profit growth collapsed by -36% [E17]. Finally, the claim of a robust multi-year foundation [E14] is undermined by the company's share price tumbling -41% over the past year [E19] and steady promoter dilution from 72.46% down to 69.90% [E33].
